{{Quote|When the ground quakes, when the smokers burn&mdash;it's their remnant acting in sympathy with their wishes. Their wishes that we honor them, and hate the Otherside!|Izri Dazh, to Adari Vaal|<ref name="skyborn" />}}
In the [[Keshiri religion]], the '''Otherside''' were the enemies of the [[Keshiri/Legends|Keshiri]] [[Deity/Legends|gods]], the [[Skyborn]]. Said to have come "from below," the Otherside engaged in a [[Great Battle]] with the Skyborn in the [[Star/Legends|stars]] above the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh]] in ancient [[Time/Legends|times]]. The Otherside were defeated in the clash, but not before they wounded the Skyborn&mdash;injured, the Skyborn spilled [[Blood/Legends|blood]] onto Kesh's [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]], creating all of the world's landmass. The legend of the Otherside continued to be told on Kesh for ages, and members of the Keshiri [[Species/Legends|species]] were always warned to hate the Otherside. Along with the Skyborn, the Otherside were eliminated from Keshiri mythology after the arrival on Kesh of a [[Lost Tribe of Sith|group]] of crash-landed [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] in [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], who did away with those stories in favor of earlier tales of the Protectors and the [[Destructors]].

==Mythology==
{{Quote|Your words glorify the Otherside, Adari Vaal.|Izri Dazh, to Adari Vaal|<ref name="skyborn" />}}
The Otherside were a group of [[Deity/Legends|deities]] depicted in the mythology of the [[Keshiri religion]], native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh]]. The Otherside, who came "from below," were said to be the nefarious enemies of the benevolent [[Skyborn]], and their conflict eventually led to a calamitous [[Great Battle|battle]] in the [[Star/Legends|stars]] above Kesh. The Great Battle, as it was known, lasted for eons&mdash;although the Otherside wounded the Skyborn, their opponents won the battle. Drops of Skyborn [[Blood/Legends|blood]] fell onto the [[Ocean/Legends|seas]] of Kesh, creating all of the planet's landmass. In the ages afterward, the Otherside were regarded as the source of all evil on the planet Kesh, and heresy against the Skyborn was said to be glorification of the Otherside. As such, the [[Keshiri/Legends|Keshiri]] regarded it as the will of the Skyborn that they were to hate the Otherside. Among the [[uvak]] beast-riding ruling council known as the [[Neshtovar]], falling from one's mount was to be claimed by the Otherside.<ref name="skyborn" />

==History==
By [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], the worship of the Skyborn, and as a result, the hatred of the Otherside, was a dominant facet in Keshiri daily life. Tradition held that in ages past, the uvak-riding Neshtovar brought the knowledge of the Otherside and the Great Battle to the masses from the [[Takara Mountains|Cetajan Mountains]]. Although faith in the Keshiri religion was prevalent, by 5000 BBY the Neshtovar still had not hammered down exactly who or what the Otherside were. That [[Standard year/Legends|year]], [[Geology|geologist]] [[Adari Vaal]] was brought before the Neshtovar to testify about the veracity of her controversial teachings of the formation of Kesh's landmass, which conflicted with the common Keshiri religion. There, Neshtovar leader [[Izri Dazh]] accused her of glorifying the Otherside with her supposed heresy. After harassment by other Keshiri, Vaal fled into the Cetajan [[Mountain/Legends|Mountains]], where she found a [[Lost Tribe of Sith|group]] of crash-landed [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] who claimed to be the Skyborn returned to Kesh.<ref name="skyborn" /> After taking control over Kesh, the Sith did away with the use of the terms "Otherside" and "Skyborn" in favor of earlier tales of the [[Destructors]] and Protectors, respectively.<ref name="paragon">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Paragon]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The Otherside were first mentioned in [[John Jackson Miller]]'s [[2009]] [[eBook]], ''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Skyborn]]''.<ref name="skyborn" />
